\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عمو} ('amu)}{عمو ('amu)}]{\fa{عمو} ('amu) — an uncle (father's brother)}

\label{lesson:FA-C500-amu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for sleepy, then the Persian for to oversleep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عمو}}
\textbf{\fa{عمو}} (\emph{'amu}) — \textquotedblleft{}an uncle (father's brother)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عموی} \fa{من} \fa{در} \fa{روستا} \fa{زندگی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'amu-ye man dar rustâ zendegi mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle lives in a village.
\end{quote}

The father's brother; the mother's brother is \emph{dâyi}. Children also call any friendly older man \emph{'amu}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'amu} comes from Arabic \emph{ʿamm}, 'paternal uncle' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'amu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'amu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'amu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for sleepy, then the Persian for to oversleep, then say \emph{'amu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عمو} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An uncle (father's brother)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عمه} ('amme)}{عمه ('amme)}]{\fa{عمه} ('amme) — an aunt (father's sister)}

\label{lesson:FA-C500-amme}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to oversleep, then the Persian for an uncle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عمه}}
\textbf{\fa{عمه}} (\emph{'amme}) — \textquotedblleft{}an aunt (father's sister)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عمه} \fa{من} \fa{آشپز} \fa{خوبی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'amme-ye man âshpaz-e khubi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My aunt is a good cook.
\end{quote}

The father's sister; the mother's sister is \emph{khâle}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'amme} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ʿamma}, 'paternal aunt' (EtymDB), the feminine of the word behind \emph{'amu}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to oversleep, then the Persian for an uncle, then say \emph{'amme} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پسرعمو} (pesar'amu)}{پسرعمو (pesar'amu)}]{\fa{پسرعمو} (pesar'amu) — a paternal cousin (son of a father's brother)}

\label{lesson:FA-C500-pesaramu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an uncle, then the Persian for an aunt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پسرعمو}}
\textbf{\fa{پسرعمو}} (\emph{pesar'amu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a paternal cousin (son of a father's brother)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پسرعمویم} \fa{با} \fa{من} \fa{همکلاسی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pesar'amuyam bâ man hamkelâsi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My cousin is in my class.
\end{quote}

\emph{pesar} 'son' + \emph{'amu}. Persian names each cousin by the parent: \emph{dokhtar'amme}, \emph{pesardâyi} and so on.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pesar'amu} is built in Persian on native \emph{pesar}, 'son', and \emph{'amu}, which comes from Arabic \emph{ʿamm}, 'paternal uncle' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pesar'amu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pesar'amu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pesar'amu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an uncle, then the Persian for an aunt, then say \emph{pesar'amu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{پسرعمو} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A paternal cousin (son of a father's brother)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دخترخاله} (dokhtarkhâle)}{دخترخاله (dokhtarkhâle)}]{\fa{دخترخاله} (dokhtarkhâle) — a maternal cousin (daughter of a mother's sister)}

\label{lesson:FA-C500-dokhtarkhale}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an aunt, then the Persian for a paternal cousin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دخترخاله}}
\textbf{\fa{دخترخاله}} (\emph{dokhtarkhâle}) — \textquotedblleft{}a maternal cousin (daughter of a mother's sister)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دخترخاله} \fa{من} \fa{دانشجوی} \fa{پزشکی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dokhtarkhâle-ye man dâneshju-ye pezeshki ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My cousin is a medical student.
\end{quote}

\emph{dokhtar} 'daughter' + \emph{khâle} 'maternal aunt'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dokhtarkhâle} is built in Persian on native \emph{dokhtar}, 'daughter', and \emph{khâle}, 'maternal aunt', which was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḫāla}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dokhtarkhâle}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an aunt, then the Persian for a paternal cousin, then say \emph{dokhtarkhâle} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خواهرزاده} (khâharzâde)}{خواهرزاده (khâharzâde)}]{\fa{خواهرزاده} (khâharzâde) — a sister's child, a nephew or niece}

\label{lesson:FA-C500-khaharzade}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a paternal cousin, then the Persian for a maternal cousin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خواهرزاده}}
\textbf{\fa{خواهرزاده}} (\emph{khâharzâde}) — \textquotedblleft{}a sister's child, a nephew or niece\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خواهرزاده} \fa{من} \fa{سه} \fa{ساله} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khâharzâde-ye man se sâle ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My nephew is three.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâhar} 'sister' + \emph{zâde} 'born of'. One word for a sister's son or daughter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâharzâde} is built on two inherited words: \emph{khâhar}, 'sister', a cousin of Latin \emph{soror} (EtymDB), and \emph{zâde}, 'born of', which EtymDB derives from \emph{zâdan}, 'to give birth' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâharzâde}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khâharzâde}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a paternal cousin, then the Persian for a maternal cousin, then say \emph{khâharzâde} again
\end{itemize}
